D: A divorced couple team up to stop their daughter from marrying a man she just met in Bali.
P: Serve the mains when both families sit down together in Bali.
S: Chicken thighs marinated in turmeric, lemongrass and coconut milk, grilled on skewers until charred, with a lime and peanut sauce.
Nori sheets brushed with sesame oil, sprinkled with sesame seeds and salt, toasted in a dry pan until crisp and cut into strips.
David and Georgia's beer pong comeback
Prawn crackers fried in hot oil for a few seconds until they puff, drained and served with sweet chilli sauce.
M: Day-old rice fried hot with chicken, garlic, chilli and kecap manis until smoky, topped with a fried egg and cucumber.
the beach where Lily falls for Gede
Snapper fillets rubbed with turmeric, chilli, garlic and lime, wrapped in banana leaves and grilled 10 minutes, with steamed rice.

Coconut water and pineapple juice with lime and mint over ice.

s.how: Marinate 600g chicken thigh strips in coconut milk, turmeric and chopped lemongrass for 2 hours. Thread onto skewers and grill until charred. Warm peanut butter with more coconut milk and lime juice for a thick sauce.

s.note: David and Georgia's beer pong comeback
s.how: Heat oil to 190C and drop in prawn crackers a few at a time. They puff up in seconds. Scoop out and drain on paper. Pile into a big bowl with sweet chilli sauce for dipping, and keep the ping pong balls well away.

m.how: Stir-fry 400g diced chicken thighs with crushed garlic and chopped red chilli in a very hot wok. Add 4 cups cold cooked jasmine rice and 3 tbsp kecap manis and toss until smoky. Serve topped with a fried egg and cucumber slices.

w.how: Soak 200g black rice overnight, then simmer in 1L water for 40 minutes until thick and soft. Stir in palm sugar to taste. Warm coconut milk with a pinch of salt and pour over each bowl. A Balinese breakfast as dessert.

d.note: sunsets over the beach in Bali
d.how: Fill tall glasses with ice and mint leaves. Pour in equal parts coconut water and pineapple juice, then squeeze in a wedge of lime. Stir and serve cold, watching the sun go down on a beach in Bali.
